intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an outdoor sunrise yoga session along the scenic Campuhan Ridge Walk in Ubud, surrounded by lush jungle and rice paddies. Many local instructors offer small group sessions here, blending breathwork and asana with Bali's natural beauty. A deeply restorative and affordable experience.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf Lesson
experiences.description: Take a beginner-friendly surf lesson on the golden sands of Seminyak Beach, one of Bali's most beautiful and accessible surf spots. After your lesson, relax and watch the legendary Bali sunset with a fresh coconut in hand. Instructors are plentiful and lessons typically include board rental.

experiences.name: Multi-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Spend several sessions at The Yoga Barn, Ubud's most iconic wellness center offering daily classes in Hatha, Vinyasa, Yin, and meditation. With a flexible drop-in class pass, you can attend multiple sessions over your 13-day stay. The jungle setting and community atmosphere make it a transformative experience.

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Menjangan Island
experiences.description: Take a day trip to Menjangan Island in West Bali National Park, home to some of Bali's most pristine coral reefs and crystal-clear waters. Snorkel alongside sea turtles, reef sharks, and vibrant tropical fish in a protected marine environment. The calm, shallow waters make it ideal for all skill levels.
experiences.location: Menjangan Island, West Bali National Park

experiences.name: Traditional Balinese Cooking Class & Market Tour
experiences.description: Start your morning at a local market in Ubud selecting fresh spices, tropical fruits, and local ingredients with your guide. Then head to an open-air kitchen to learn how to prepare classic Balinese dishes like Nasi Goreng, Satay Lilit, and Lawar. A delicious cultural immersion that connects food, tradition, and community.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and customs, then take a pre-booked budget shuttle or shared taxi (~IDR 150,000–200,000) to Campuhan Ridge, Ubud. Check in to Campuhan Ridge Ubud Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a gentle stroll along the iconic Campuhan Ridge Walk — a free, scenic 2 km trail through lush green hills and rice paddies right from the doorstep.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearby Campuhan and Penestanan village area on foot. Visit a local warung for a relaxed first dinner in Bali. Rest early to recover from the flight.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a light meal at the airport or a roadside warung on the way to Ubud (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.dinner: Warung Babi Guling or a local warung near Campuhan — try nasi campur or mie goreng (~IDR 35,000–60,000)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after the 13:00 arrival. The Campuhan Ridge Walk is free and starts very close to the hotel — perfect for a gentle first-afternoon stretch after the flight. Pre-book your airport shuttle in advance for the best budget rate.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise Campuhan Ridge Walk (free). The golden morning light over the hills is breathtaking and the trail is quiet at dawn. Return to the hotel for breakfast. Afterward, walk or rent a bicycle (~IDR 50,000/day) to explore the Penestanan artists' village and its charming lanes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary in central Ubud (~IDR 80,000 entry). Spend 1.5–2 hours wandering through the ancient forest temples and observing the resident macaques. Then browse Ubud Art Market (Pasar Seni Ubud) for affordable local crafts, sarongs, and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Jalan Hanoman and Jalan Dewisita for an evening stroll. Catch a free or low-cost traditional Kecak or Legong dance performance at Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) — tickets around IDR 100,000–150,000.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café near Campuhan — try bubur ayam (rice porridge) or banana pancakes (~IDR 25,000–50,000)
meals.lunch: Warung near Monkey Forest — nasi goreng or gado-gado (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.dinner: Warung Teges or a local warung on Jalan Hanoman — babi guling or sate lilit (~IDR 40,000–70,000)

day_by_day.notes: The Campuhan Ridge Walk is best done before 8:00 AM to avoid heat and crowds. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water. Modest dress (sarong) is required to enter the Monkey Forest temples — sarongs are provided at the entrance.

day_by_day.morning: Join an affordable morning yoga class at one of Ubud's budget-friendly studios such as Yoga Barn or Radiantly Alive (~IDR 120,000–150,000 per drop-in class). These are within cycling or walking distance from Campuhan. Enjoy the post-yoga calm with a healthy smoothie bowl at a nearby café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tegalalang Rice Terraces (~15 min by scooter from Ubud, ~IDR 10,000–20,000 entry donation). Walk the terraced paths, take photos, and interact with local farmers. Rent a scooter for the day (~IDR 70,000–100,000) for flexibility. Stop at a roadside stall for fresh coconut water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud and visit the Ubud Night Market (Pasar Malam Ubud) near the main market area for cheap and delicious local street food and fresh produce.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or acai bowl at a café near the yoga studio (~IDR 45,000–70,000)
meals.lunch: Warung at or near Tegalalang — nasi campur (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.dinner: Ubud Night Market street food — satay, martabak, fresh fruit (~IDR 30,000–60,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: Book yoga classes in advance or arrive 15 minutes early for drop-in spots. Tegalalang has a small entry donation — carry small bills. Wear a helmet when riding a scooter and check that your travel insurance covers scooter use.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning trip to Tirta Empul Temple (~20 min by scooter), one of Bali's most sacred water temples. Participate in or observe the traditional purification ritual in the holy spring pools. Entry ~IDR 50,000. Arrive by 8:00 AM before tour groups arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Gunung Kawi Temple complex (~10 min away) — ancient 11th-century rock-cut shrines carved into a cliff face (~IDR 50,000 entry). Walk down the steep stone steps through lush jungle. Afterward, stop at a local warung in the village of Tampaksiring for lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud. Visit Yoga Barn's evening community class or meditation session (~IDR 120,000). Enjoy a quiet evening walk along the Campuhan Ridge as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at hotel or a local café before departing — toast and coffee (~IDR 25,000–40,000)
meals.lunch: Local warung in Tampaksiring village — nasi campur or soto ayam (~IDR 30,000–45,000)
meals.dinner: Warung near Campuhan or hotel area — grilled fish or tempeh (~IDR 40,000–65,000)

day_by_day.notes: A sarong is mandatory at Tirta Empul — provided at the entrance. If you wish to join the purification ritual, wear modest clothing you don't mind getting wet. Arrive early to both sites to avoid crowds and midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the beach! Take a budget tourist shuttle from Ubud to Seminyak or Canggu (~IDR 50,000–80,000 one way). Arrive by mid-morning and head to Batu Bolong Beach in Canggu — a relaxed, less commercialized beach popular with surfers and yogis. Enjoy the warm July weather (avg high 25°C, low rain).
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a surfboard and take a beginner surf lesson at one of Canggu's budget surf schools (~IDR 150,000–200,000 for a 1.5-hour lesson including board). Relax on the beach between sessions. Explore the Canggu beach walk and local warungs.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Bali sunset from the beach. Head to a budget-friendly beach bar for a fresh juice or Bintang beer. Take the evening shuttle back to Ubud or stay overnight in Canggu if budget allows.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or café in Ubud before departure — banana pancakes (~IDR 30,000–45,000)
meals.lunch: Warung on Batu Bolong Beach — grilled corn, nasi goreng, fresh coconut (~IDR 40,000–65,000)
meals.dinner: Warung or budget café in Canggu — Buddha bowl or nasi campur (~IDR 45,000–75,000)

day_by_day.notes: July is a great month for surfing in Canggu — waves are consistent but manageable for beginners. Apply strong sunscreen and stay hydrated. Book the shuttle the night before from your hotel or a local travel agent for the best rate.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Ubud (if you stayed in Canggu overnight, take the morning shuttle back). Morning yoga session at Yoga Barn or a free outdoor yoga session on the hotel terrace. Practice pranayama and meditation to reset after the beach day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's cultural heart — visit the Ubud Palace (free to view from outside), walk through the main market, and discover the small alleyways and local temples. Stop at the Blanco Renaissance Museum (~IDR 80,000) to see the eccentric artist Don Blanco's flamboyant paintings in a stunning Campuhan hillside setting.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Balinese cooking class — many budget options available in Ubud (~IDR 200,000–250,000) that include a market visit, cooking instruction, and a full meal. A great way to learn local cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie or yogurt bowl at a café near Campuhan (~IDR 35,000–55,000)
meals.lunch: Warung near Ubud Palace — gado-gado or lawar (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.dinner: Eat the dishes you cooked in your cooking class — included in class fee

day_by_day.notes: The Blanco Museum is right near the hotel in Campuhan — very walkable. Book the cooking class in advance; evening classes fill up quickly. Many cooking classes include a morning market visit if you prefer to join one that starts earlier.

day_by_day.morning: Trek to Kanto Lampo Waterfall or Tibumana Waterfall (~20–30 min by scooter from Ubud). These hidden jungle waterfalls are less touristy and have small entry fees (~IDR 10,000–20,000). Swim in the natural pool at the base — refreshing in the warm July weather.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Goa Gajah (Elephant Cave) temple (~IDR 50,000 entry) — an ancient 9th-century cave temple with carved stone demons at the entrance, bathing pools, and jungle surroundings. Combine with a walk to the nearby Petanu River valley.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud for a relaxing evening. Treat yourself to a budget traditional Balinese massage (~IDR 80,000–120,000 for 60 minutes) at one of the many affordable spas along Jalan Hanoman.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local warung — nasi goreng and coffee (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or warung near the waterfall — instant noodles or rice box (~IDR 20,000–40,000)
meals.dinner: Warung Ibu Oka or similar in Ubud center — babi guling (roast pork) set meal (~IDR 55,000–80,000)

day_by_day.notes: Wear water shoes or sandals with grip for the waterfall trek — rocks can be slippery. Bring a dry bag for your phone and valuables. Goa Gajah requires a sarong — provided at the entrance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day beach excursion to the Bukit Peninsula in South Bali. Take a budget shuttle to Uluwatu (~IDR 80,000–100,000). Morning visit to Uluwatu Temple — a dramatic sea cliff temple (~IDR 50,000 entry). Walk the cliff-edge path with ocean views and watch for monkeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to Padang Padang Beach (~IDR 15,000 entry) — a stunning, sheltered cove with clear turquoise water, perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Rent snorkel gear (~IDR 30,000–50,000) and explore the coral. Alternatively, walk to Suluban Beach (Blue Point) nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the famous Uluwatu Kecak Fire Dance performance at sunset at the clifftop amphitheater (~IDR 150,000). Watch the dramatic dance with the Indian Ocean as a backdrop. Return to Ubud by night shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel or café before departure — toast, eggs, coffee (~IDR 30,000–50,000)
meals.lunch: Warung at Padang Padang Beach — grilled fish, fresh coconut, nasi campur (~IDR 45,000–70,000)
meals.dinner: Warung near Uluwatu or on the way back — or eat a hearty lunch and have a light snack for dinner (~IDR 30,000–50,000)

day_by_day.notes: Book your return shuttle to Ubud in advance — last shuttles usually depart around 20:00–21:00. The Kecak Dance starts around 18:00 and lasts about 1 hour. Bring a light jacket for the evening ride back. Sarong required at Uluwatu Temple.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning. Gentle sunrise yoga on the Campuhan Ridge or at the hotel. Enjoy a slow breakfast and explore the Penestanan neighborhood's art studios and organic cafés at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Neka Art Museum (~IDR 75,000) in Campuhan — one of Bali's best collections of traditional and modern Balinese and Indonesian paintings, just a short walk from the hotel. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the galleries and lush garden setting.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the Campuhan Ridge at sunset for golden hour views. Then head to a local warung for dinner and an early night. Optional: join an evening meditation class at Yoga Barn (~IDR 120,000).

meals.breakfast: Slow café breakfast — avocado toast or fruit plate at a Penestanan café (~IDR 45,000–65,000)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from the local market — fresh fruit, tempe, and rice (~IDR 20,000–35,000)
meals.dinner: Warung near Campuhan — vegetable curry or tofu satay (~IDR 35,000–55,000)

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate lighter day to rest your feet and recharge mid-trip. The Neka Art Museum is very close to the hotel and a hidden gem — worth the small entry fee. Penestanan village is a lovely, quiet alternative to busy central Ubud.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning trip to Mount Batur for a sunrise trek. Book a budget guided trek (~IDR 350,000–450,000 including guide, which is mandatory) the night before. Depart Ubud around 02:00–03:00 AM. Reach the 1,717 m summit by sunrise (~05:30–06:00) for spectacular views over Lake Batur and Mount Agung.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the volcano and visit the natural hot springs at the base of Mount Batur (~IDR 50,000–100,000) to soak your tired muscles. Return to Ubud by early afternoon and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Light evening — gentle walk, a Balinese massage, and early dinner. Rest well after the predawn hike.

meals.breakfast: Simple snack and coffee before the trek (usually provided by guide at the summit — eggs cooked on volcanic steam!)
meals.lunch: Warung near Lake Batur after the hot springs — grilled corn, nasi goreng (~IDR 35,000–55,000)
meals.dinner: Light dinner at a warung near the hotel — soup or congee (~IDR 30,000–50,000)

day_by_day.notes: The Mount Batur sunrise trek is one of Bali's top experiences. Book through your hotel or a local agent the day before. Bring warm layers — the summit is cold before sunrise (~10–15°C). Wear sturdy shoes. The hot springs afterward are a wonderful reward.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning after the Batur trek. Sleep in, then join a late-morning restorative yoga or yin yoga class at Yoga Barn (~IDR 120,000). Focus on stretching the legs and hips after yesterday's hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the village of Penglipuran near Bangli (~45 min by scooter) — one of Bali's cleanest and most traditional villages (~IDR 30,000 entry). Walk through perfectly maintained bamboo-lined lanes and interact with locals. Stop at the nearby Tukad Cepung Waterfall (~IDR 20,000 entry) — a magical cave waterfall where sunlight streams through a hole in the cliff.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ubud. Browse the evening market for last-minute souvenirs. Enjoy a final relaxed dinner at a favorite warung.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or café — light breakfast, yogurt and fruit (~IDR 30,000–45,000)
meals.lunch: Warung in Penglipuran village — traditional Balinese set meal (~IDR 35,000–55,000)
meals.dinner: Favorite warung in Ubud — treat yourself to a slightly larger meal (~IDR 50,000–80,000)

day_by_day.notes: Tukad Cepung Waterfall involves a short but slippery cave walk through a shallow stream — wear sandals you can get wet. The waterfall is most photogenic in the morning when sunlight beams through, but it's still beautiful in the afternoon. Penglipuran village is genuinely car-free and very peaceful.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach day — head to Sanur Beach on Bali's east coast (~45 min by shuttle or scooter from Ubud, ~IDR 50,000–80,000). Sanur is calmer, less crowded, and more budget-friendly than Seminyak. Walk the famous Sanur Beach boardwalk, swim in the shallow, calm waters, and enjoy the relaxed local atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Sanur village area — visit the Le Mayeur Museum (~IDR 50,000), the home and studio of Belgian painter Adrien-Jean Le Mayeur, set in a beautiful beachside garden. Browse the local market for snacks and souvenirs. Optional: rent a bicycle along the beach path (~IDR 30,000/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Sanur Beach — the east-coast orientation means it's better for sunrises, but the evening light is still beautiful. Return to Ubud for a final evening. Pack bags and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Café in Ubud before departure — coffee and toast (~IDR 25,000–40,000)
meals.lunch: Warung on Sanur beachfront — grilled fish, plecing kangkung (water spinach), rice (~IDR 45,000–70,000)
meals.dinner: Final dinner at a favorite Ubud warung or splurge slightly at a mid-range restaurant (~IDR 60,000–100,000)

day_by_day.notes: Sanur is a great final beach day — it's quieter and more authentically local than the Seminyak/Kuta strip. The beachfront boardwalk is lovely for a slow afternoon walk. Make sure bags are packed tonight as Day 13 may involve an early checkout.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise Campuhan Ridge Walk — one last time to soak in the beauty of Ubud's hills. Return for a leisurely breakfast. Check out of the hotel. Store luggage if needed and take a final walk through Ubud's streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, explore any last spots in Ubud — revisit the market for final souvenirs, grab a fresh juice, or simply sit in a café and reflect on the trip. Head to the airport (~1.5–2 hours from Ubud by shuttle, ~IDR 150,000–200,000) with plenty of time before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final hotel or café breakfast in Ubud — treat yourself to a full Balinese breakfast (~IDR 40,000–65,000)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Ubud before departure or at the airport (~IDR 35,000–80,000)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Book your airport shuttle the night before to guarantee availability. Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight departure for the drive and check-in. Ngurah Rai International Airport can be busy — arrive early. Double-check baggage weight limits if you've bought souvenirs.

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport transfer to Campuhan Ridge, Ubud Boutique Stay (~1.5 hrs). Check in, freshen up, and take a gentle stroll along the iconic Campuhan Ridge Walk to soak in the rolling green hills and rice paddies surrounding the hotel
day_by_day.evening: Explore the quiet lanes of Campuhan village, browse local art galleries along Jalan Raya Campuhan, and settle into the Ubud atmosphere with a relaxed sunset walk

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or a roadside warung during the transfer
meals.dinner: Murni's Warung — a Ubud institution perched above the Campuhan river; try the nasi campur or grilled fish (mid-range, ~IDR 80,000–150,000 per dish)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Hydrate well and go to bed early to reset your body clock. Exchange currency at the airport or use a reputable ATM in Ubud.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session at a studio near Campuhan Ridge — try Yoga Barn or Radiantly Alive, both offering morning flow classes starting at 07:00–08:00. Enjoy the cool morning air and lush surroundings
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary in Ubud centre (~15 min from hotel). Wander the ancient temple grounds and observe the resident macaques. Afterward, explore Ubud Art Market for handcrafted souvenirs and batik textiles
day_by_day.evening: Catch a traditional Kecak fire dance performance at Pura Dalem Ubud or Arma Museum (~19:00). Book tickets in advance (~IDR 100,000–150,000 per person)

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café Pomegranate near Campuhan Ridge — fresh smoothie bowls and avocado toast
meals.lunch: Warung Ibu Oka — famous Balinese suckling pig (babi guling); queue early as it sells out (~IDR 60,000–80,000)
meals.dinner: Locavore NXT or Hujan Locale — modern Indonesian cuisine with local ingredients; budget ~IDR 200,000–350,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book yoga classes and the Kecak performance a day ahead. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Monkey Forest and market. Keep bags secure around the monkeys.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Tirta Empul Temple (~30 min from Ubud) — a sacred Hindu water temple where locals perform purification rituals in spring-fed pools. Arrive by 08:00 to beat the crowds. Dress modestly; sarongs available to rent at the gate
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Tegalalang Rice Terraces (~20 min from Ubud) for a scenic walk through the UNESCO-listed stepped paddies. Enjoy the views and stop at a hillside café for coffee overlooking the terraces
day_by_day.evening: Return to Campuhan and enjoy a traditional Balinese massage at a local spa near the hotel — try Karsa Spa or Alaya Spa (~IDR 150,000–250,000 for 60–90 min)

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local warung near Campuhan — nasi goreng or bubur ayam (rice porridge)
meals.lunch: Warung at Tegalalang — many small warungs along the rice terrace path serve Indonesian staples; ~IDR 40,000–70,000
meals.dinner: Bridges Bali — romantic restaurant perched above the Campuhan river gorge; grilled seafood and Indonesian fusion (~IDR 200,000–350,000)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a local driver for the day (~IDR 400,000–600,000) to visit Tirta Empul and Tegalalang comfortably. Bring a light rain jacket — afternoon showers are possible even in dry season.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike up Mount Batur volcano (~1.5 hrs from Ubud). Depart by 03:30 from the hotel to reach the summit by sunrise (~05:30). A guided trek is mandatory (~IDR 400,000–600,000 including guide). Witness the sun rising over the caldera lake — unforgettable
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and soak in natural hot springs at the base of Batur (~IDR 100,000–150,000). Return to Ubud by early afternoon and rest at the hotel
day_by_day.evening: Gentle restorative yoga class at Yoga Barn in the late afternoon (~17:00). Afterward, a quiet evening stroll along Campuhan Ridge at dusk

meals.breakfast: Simple packed breakfast provided by most Batur guides at the summit — instant noodles, banana, and tea/coffee
meals.lunch: Warung near the hot springs or stop at a local restaurant on the way back to Ubud
meals.dinner: Naughty Nuri's Warung — famous for BBQ ribs and cold Bintang beer; casual and lively (~IDR 100,000–200,000)

day_by_day.notes: Mount Batur hike is moderately strenuous — wear layers as it is cold at the summit (around 10–15°C). Book your guide the day before through the hotel. Rest well the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yin yoga or meditation class at Radiantly Alive (~08:00). Spend the rest of the morning exploring Campuhan Ridge Walk at a leisurely pace — the golden morning light is perfect for photography
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Blanco Renaissance Museum (~10 min walk from hotel) — the flamboyant home-studio of Spanish-Balinese artist Don Antonio Blanco, with stunning river gorge views. Then explore Penestanan village's artist colony and boutique galleries
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Legong dance performance at Ubud Palace (Puri Saren) in central Ubud (~19:30). Tickets ~IDR 100,000–150,000

meals.breakfast: Seniman Coffee Studio — specialty coffee and healthy breakfast bowls; a favourite among the Ubud creative community
meals.lunch: Clear Café — organic, health-conscious menu perfect for yoga enthusiasts; try the rainbow salad or tempeh bowl (~IDR 80,000–140,000)
meals.dinner: Mozaic Restaurant — one of Ubud's finest; French-Indonesian tasting menus. Splurge slightly for a special evening (~IDR 500,000–800,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 5 is intentionally relaxed — a recovery day after the Batur hike. Embrace the slow pace of Ubud. Book Mozaic well in advance if choosing to dine there.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer from Ubud to Seminyak (~1.5 hrs). Check in to a mid-range boutique hotel in Seminyak (e.g., The Layar or Katamama area). Head straight to Seminyak Beach for a morning swim and beach walk
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Seminyak's boutique shopping strip along Jalan Laksmana (Eat Street) — browse local fashion, homeware, and surf shops. Visit Biku or Petitenget area for a relaxed afternoon coffee
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Seminyak sunset at Ku De Ta (now ARTOTEL Sunset Road area) or Potato Head Beach Club — order a cocktail and enjoy the golden hour on the beach

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or grab something on the road during transfer
meals.lunch: Warung Nia — beloved local spot near Seminyak; generous portions of Balinese food at very reasonable prices (~IDR 50,000–80,000)
meals.dinner: Merah Putih — stunning two-storey restaurant in a dramatic bamboo pavilion; modern Indonesian cuisine (~IDR 200,000–400,000)

day_by_day.notes: Seminyak is more beach-and-lifestyle focused compared to Ubud. The vibe shifts from spiritual to social. Pack your swimwear and sunscreen. July is peak season — book restaurants for dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga on the beach or join a beach yoga class offered by several studios near Seminyak (~07:00). Afterward, enjoy a morning swim at Seminyak or Petitenget Beach before the crowds arrive
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Tanah Lot Temple (~45 min from Seminyak) — one of Bali's most photographed sea temples perched on a coastal rock. Explore the surrounding clifftop and temple grounds
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Tanah Lot (one of the best sunset spots in Bali) then return to Seminyak for dinner

meals.breakfast: Revolver Espresso — Seminyak's cult coffee spot; excellent flat whites and açaí bowls in a laneway setting
meals.lunch: Local warung near Tanah Lot — simple nasi campur or mie goreng (~IDR 35,000–60,000)
meals.dinner: Sarong Restaurant — intimate and beautifully designed; Indonesian and Asian tapas style (~IDR 200,000–350,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is very popular at sunset — arrive by 17:00 to secure a good viewing spot. Entry fee ~IDR 60,000 per person. Sarong is one of Seminyak's most celebrated restaurants; reserve ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Surf lesson at Seminyak or Kuta Beach (~09:00) — beginner-friendly waves and several reputable surf schools offering 2-hour lessons (~IDR 250,000–400,000 including board and instructor)
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at a beach club — try Potato Head Beach Club or W Bali's Woobar for pool and beach access with a day pass. Enjoy the sun, sea, and a light lunch poolside
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kerobokan's restaurant and art gallery scene. Visit Deus Ex Machina — a legendary concept store combining motorcycles, surfboards, and a café/bar with live music some evenings

meals.breakfast: Baked Goods at Sisterfields Café — popular brunch spot; smashed avo, eggs benedict, and great coffee (~IDR 100,000–160,000)
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch — burgers, salads, or grilled fish at the poolside bar (~IDR 100,000–200,000)
meals.dinner: Deus Ex Machina café or nearby Shelter Restaurant — relaxed, quality food in a cool setting (~IDR 100,000–200,000)

day_by_day.notes: Surf lessons are best in the morning when winds are calmer. Apply reef-safe sunscreen. Beach clubs can have minimum spend requirements — check before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer to Canggu (~20 min from Seminyak). Spend the morning at Batu Bolong or Echo Beach — popular with surfers and digital nomads. Watch experienced surfers or try renting a board if confident
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Canggu village — browse the eclectic mix of surf shops, vegan cafés, and rice paddy paths. Visit Berawa Beach and walk north along the coastline
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seminyak for sunset drinks at La Plancha — a bohemian beachfront bar with colourful bean bags on the sand; perfect for a relaxed sunset session

meals.breakfast: Old Man's Canggu — iconic beach bar and café; great breakfast burritos and smoothie bowls with ocean views
meals.lunch: The Shady Shack — beloved plant-based restaurant in Canggu; wholesome bowls, smoothies, and fresh juices (~IDR 80,000–140,000)
meals.dinner: Métis Restaurant, Seminyak — elegant French-Indonesian fusion in a beautiful garden setting (~IDR 250,000–450,000)

day_by_day.notes: Canggu is a 20–30 minute drive from Seminyak depending on traffic. Rent a scooter (~IDR 60,000–80,000/day) if comfortable riding, or use a Grab/Gojek app for easy transfers.

day_by_day.morning: Transfer to Uluwatu (~1 hour from Seminyak). Check in to a clifftop guesthouse or stay at a mid-range hotel in the Bingin/Padang Padang area. Visit Uluwatu Temple perched dramatically on a 70m sea cliff — arrive early to beat tour groups
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Padang Padang Beach — one of Bali's most beautiful hidden beaches accessed via a narrow cave entrance. Swim, snorkel, or simply relax on the white sand
day_by_day.evening: Return to Uluwatu Temple for the famous Kecak fire dance performed at sunset on the clifftop stage (~18:00). Tickets ~IDR 150,000 per person. The ocean backdrop makes this one of Bali's most spectacular performances

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a warung near Seminyak before departure
meals.lunch: Single Fin Bar & Restaurant, Uluwatu — legendary clifftop bar overlooking Uluwatu surf break; burgers, tacos, and cold drinks with a stunning view (~IDR 100,000–200,000)
meals.dinner: Cashew Tree, Bingin — relaxed garden restaurant serving Mediterranean and Indonesian food; popular with surfers and yogis (~IDR 80,000–160,000)

day_by_day.notes: Beware of monkeys at Uluwatu Temple — they are notorious for snatching sunglasses, phones, and bags. Secure all valuables. The Kecak performance is weather-dependent; confirm on the day.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga on a clifftop deck — several retreat centres in Bingin and Uluwatu offer morning classes with ocean views (~07:00). Afterward, head to Bingin Beach for a morning swim in the turquoise water
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Dreamland Beach and Thomas Beach — less crowded alternatives in the Bukit Peninsula. Walk between beaches along the coastal paths and enjoy the dramatic limestone cliff scenery
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner at Ulu Cliffhouse or Omnia Dayclub (Uluwatu) — upscale clifftop venues with infinity pools and panoramic Indian Ocean views. Dress code applies; budget for cocktails (~IDR 150,000–250,000 each)

meals.breakfast: Drifter Café or a local warung in Bingin — smoothie bowls, eggs, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Warung on Bingin Beach — fresh grilled fish, satay, and cold coconuts served steps from the water (~IDR 50,000–90,000)
meals.dinner: Kismet, Uluwatu — stylish restaurant and bar with a Mediterranean-leaning menu and great cocktails (~IDR 150,000–280,000)

day_by_day.notes: The Bukit Peninsula beaches require descending steep staircases — wear appropriate footwear. Tides affect beach access at Bingin and Dreamland; check tide times. Apply sunscreen liberally.

day_by_day.morning: Morning snorkelling trip from Nusa Dua or Sanur (~45 min from Uluwatu). Book a half-day guided snorkelling tour to explore coral reefs and tropical fish (~IDR 300,000–500,000 including equipment and guide)
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Sanur for a relaxed afternoon on Sanur Beach — calmer waters than the west coast, ideal for swimming and paddleboarding. Rent a SUP board (~IDR 100,000/hr) and paddle along the coastline
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Sanur's charming beachfront promenade at sunset. Browse the evening market stalls and enjoy the laid-back atmosphere of this traditional fishing village

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a beachside café in Uluwatu before departure
meals.lunch: Char Ming, Sanur — beautiful garden restaurant in a restored colonial villa; Balinese and Indonesian cuisine (~IDR 100,000–200,000)
meals.dinner: Massimo Il Ristorante, Sanur — beloved Italian restaurant run by an Italian chef; excellent pasta, pizza, and gelato (~IDR 120,000–220,000)

day_by_day.notes: Sanur is quieter and more local in feel than Seminyak or Canggu — a lovely contrast for the penultimate evening. The beachfront promenade is perfect for an evening walk. Check ferry schedules if planning a day trip to Nusa Penida.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along Sanur Beach promenade — one of Bali's best sunrise spots on the east-facing coast. Enjoy a last morning yoga session on the beach or at a nearby studio. Pack and check out of accommodation
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Sanur Market or head back through Seminyak for any remaining shopping. Transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport (~30–45 min from Sanur depending on traffic). Allow at least 3 hours before departure
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Ngurah Rai International Airport

meals.breakfast: Porch Café, Sanur — a local favourite for its generous breakfasts and strong coffee; a perfect final Bali morning meal
meals.lunch: Warung Mak Beng, Sanur — legendary local warung serving one dish only: fried fish with soup and rice. A Bali institution since 1941 (~IDR 50,000). Arrive early — it fills up fast
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a final meal near the airport if time permits

day_by_day.notes: Sanur to the airport is approximately 30–45 minutes. Add extra time during peak hours (15:00–18:00). Confirm your flight details and any liquid/item restrictions for carry-on. Keep a small amount of IDR for airport tips or last-minute purchases. Selamat jalan — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Campuhan Ridge, Ubud Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the iconic Campuhan Ridge Walk to soak in the lush green valley views and settle into the Ubud ambiance
day_by_day.evening: Gentle welcome yoga session on the hotel's private terrace or garden as the sun sets over the ridge, followed by a relaxing soak and spa welcome treatment at the property

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or at airport
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments and tropical fruit platter arranged by the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bridges Bali — an iconic fine-dining restaurant perched above the Campuhan River gorge, offering contemporary Asian-European cuisine with dramatic jungle views. Try the slow-roasted duck or fresh seafood tasting menu paired with curated wines

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance through the hotel concierge. Keep Day 1 light to recover from the flight. The Campuhan Ridge Walk is a 10-minute walk from the hotel and is best enjoyed in the late afternoon golden light.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the Campuhan Ridge with a private certified instructor — practice pranayama and flow yoga as the mist lifts over the valley. Follow with a nourishing smoothie bowl and herbal tea at the hotel
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Neka Art Museum and Puri Lukisan Museum in central Ubud to immerse yourself in traditional and contemporary Balinese art. Hire a private guide for deeper cultural context. Browse the boutique galleries and artisan shops along Jalan Raya Ubud
day_by_day.evening: Attend the legendary Kecak Fire Dance performance at Pura Dalem Ubud or Arma Open Stage — a mesmerizing Balinese ritual dance performed at dusk

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel — fresh tropical fruits, Balinese black rice porridge, eggs Benedict, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at Locavore NXT — Ubud's celebrated farm-to-table concept restaurant using hyper-local ingredients. Reserve ahead
meals.dinner: Dinner at Room4Dessert or Mozaic Restaurant Ubud — Mozaic offers a world-class tasting menu with French-Balinese fusion in a romantic garden setting

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kecak Dance tickets in advance. Mozaic requires reservations at least 2–3 days ahead. The private yoga instructor can be arranged through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise tour to Tegallalang Rice Terraces — arrive early before crowds, walk the terraces with a local guide, and learn about the traditional Subak irrigation system. Enjoy the cool morning air and dramatic green landscapes
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the sacred Tirta Empul Temple for a purification water blessing ceremony — a deeply spiritual Balinese experience. Then explore the nearby Gunung Kawi royal monument carved into volcanic rock
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a luxurious two-hour Balinese massage and body scrub treatment at the in-house spa or a premium spa nearby such as COMO Shambhala Estate

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure — fresh fruit, yogurt parfait, and Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sari Organik — a charming organic farm restaurant nestled in the rice fields of Ubud, accessible by a scenic walk through the paddies
meals.dinner: Dinner at Swept Away at COMO Uma Ubud — elegant open-air dining with refined Indonesian cuisine and an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Bring a sarong and sash for the temple visit — these can be borrowed on-site but having your own is more comfortable. Start the morning excursion by 6:00 AM for the best light and fewest crowds at Tegallalang.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Yin yoga and meditation class at The Yoga Barn — Ubud's most prestigious wellness center. Choose from their curated schedule of expert-led classes in a beautiful jungle-surrounded studio
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cooking class with a Balinese chef — visit a local market to select fresh ingredients, then prepare a traditional Balinese feast including satay lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at Karsa Kafe overlooking the Campuhan Ridge, followed by a private romantic dinner set up in the hotel garden or terrace under the stars

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — avocado toast on sourdough, poached eggs, tropical fruit platter, and Balinese cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch included as part of the cooking class experience
meals.dinner: Private in-hotel dinner or at Alaya Resort Ubud's Plantation Restaurant — refined Indonesian flavors in a lush garden setting

day_by_day.notes: The Yoga Barn class schedule changes weekly — check and book online in advance. The private cooking class can be arranged through the hotel concierge and typically lasts 4–5 hours including the market visit.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Seminyak and Petitenget Beach — depart early with a private driver. Enjoy the pristine beach, swim in calm July waters, and relax on premium sunbeds at a luxury beach club
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon at Potato Head Beach Club or Ku De Ta — enjoy the infinity pool, creative cocktails, and the vibrant yet refined beach club atmosphere. Explore the boutique design shops along Jalan Petitenget
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner in Seminyak — watch the famous Bali sunset from the beach before heading to dinner

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Potato Head Beach Club — their menu features creative Asian and Western dishes with fresh seafood and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sarong Restaurant Seminyak — one of Bali's most awarded restaurants, offering a Pan-Asian tasting menu in a stunning colonial-inspired setting

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Ubud to Seminyak takes approximately 1–1.5 hours. Arrange a private driver for the full day. July weather is ideal for beach days with minimal rain and warm temperatures around 25°C.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga on the Campuhan Ridge Walk — self-guided mindful walk with a personal yoga mat session at the ridge viewpoint. Return for a luxurious hotel breakfast
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Goa Gajah (Elephant Cave) — an 11th-century archaeological site and Hindu sanctuary with intricate carvings and bathing pools. Then explore the artisan village of Mas, renowned for its master woodcarvers
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Legong dance performance at Puri Saren Agung (Ubud Royal Palace) — held in the royal courtyard under torch light

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the hotel — Balinese-style nasi goreng, fresh juices, tropical fruits, and artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Lunch at Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka — the most celebrated suckling pig restaurant in Ubud, a cultural institution beloved by food lovers worldwide
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hujan Locale — a sophisticated Indonesian restaurant celebrating regional cuisines from across the archipelago with a modern presentation and craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: The Legong performance at Ubud Royal Palace typically begins at 19:30 and lasts about one hour. Purchase tickets at the venue or through your hotel concierge. Dress modestly for temple visits.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to East Bali — depart early for Mount Agung and Besakih Temple (Mother Temple of Bali), the most sacred and largest temple complex on the island, dramatically set on the slopes of the volcano
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Tirtagangga Water Palace — a stunning royal garden with ornamental pools, fountains, and lush grounds. Take a dip in the freshwater pools surrounded by tropical gardens
day_by_day.evening: Scenic drive back to Ubud via the coastal road with stops at rice terrace viewpoints. Arrive back in time for a restorative hotel spa treatment

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local warung near Tirtagangga — fresh grilled fish, steamed rice, and local vegetables with coconut sambal
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kafe Batan Waru in Ubud — a beloved institution serving authentic Balinese and Indonesian dishes in a warm, intimate atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The drive to East Bali takes approximately 2 hours. Hire a knowledgeable private guide for Besakih as the temple complex is large and complex. Bring a light jacket as the altitude near Besakih can be cooler.

day_by_day.morning: Private Ashtanga yoga masterclass at a boutique studio in Ubud — work with a senior teacher for a personalized 90-minute session focused on alignment, breathwork, and advanced postures
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ubud Monkey Forest (Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary) — a lush nature reserve and Hindu temple complex inhabited by over 700 Balinese long-tailed macaques. Walk the shaded forest paths
day_by_day.evening: Luxury river valley walk and sundowner experience — guided walk down to the Campuhan River followed by cocktails at Karsa Kafe as the sun sets over the ridge

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga breakfast at the hotel — smoothie bowl, banana, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Post-yoga brunch at Alchemy Ubud — Bali's premier raw vegan and organic restaurant with creative plant-based dishes and superfood elixirs
meals.dinner: Dinner at Aperitif Restaurant and Bar at Viceroy Bali — an award-winning fine dining experience with a European-inspired tasting menu and one of Bali's finest wine and cocktail programs

day_by_day.notes: Aperitif at Viceroy Bali is one of the most prestigious dining experiences in Ubud — reserve at least one week in advance. Smart casual dress code applies. The yoga masterclass should be booked through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nusa Penida — take a private speedboat from Sanur Beach (approximately 1.5-hour drive from Ubud). Visit the iconic Kelingking Beach viewpoint — one of Bali's most photographed cliffs — and the crystal-clear waters of Crystal Bay
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling at Manta Point to swim with majestic manta rays in their natural habitat — a once-in-a-lifetime experience. July is peak manta ray season
day_by_day.evening: Return speedboat to Sanur, private transfer back to Ubud. Relaxing evening at the hotel with a private in-room dinner and a soothing foot reflexology treatment

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast provided by the hotel for the early departure
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beachside warung on Nusa Penida — grilled fish, lobster, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Private in-room dining at the hotel — curated Balinese tasting menu delivered to your room or terrace

day_by_day.notes: Book a private speedboat charter for this excursion — avoid crowded public boats. The speedboat departs from Sanur around 8:00 AM. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a rash guard, and motion sickness tablets if needed. Manta ray sightings are highly likely in July.

day_by_day.morning: Restorative morning — sleep in, followed by a gentle Restorative yoga and sound healing session at the hotel or The Yoga Barn. Enjoy the peaceful hotel grounds and pool
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the village of Penestanan — Ubud's 'Artists' Village' — on foot or by bicycle. Visit working artist studios, contemporary galleries, and charming cafes along quiet village lanes
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the famous Pura Tanah Lot sea temple — a 1.5-hour drive from Ubud but absolutely worth the trip for the dramatic ocean-top temple silhouette at golden hour

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full breakfast at the hotel — eggs your way, fresh pastries, tropical fruits, Balinese coffee, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cafe Pomegranate or Seniman Coffee Studio — artisan coffee and fresh light bites in a creative Ubud setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Merah Putih in Seminyak (en route back from Tanah Lot) — stunning colonial-style restaurant with creative modern Indonesian cuisine and an impressive cocktail menu

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is best visited 30–45 minutes before sunset. The drive from Ubud takes approximately 1.5 hours — coordinate with your private driver. Entry requires a sarong.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike to the summit of Mount Batur — depart at 02:00 AM for the 2-hour guided trek to the crater rim, arriving at the summit for a breathtaking sunrise above the clouds over Lake Batur and Mount Agung
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a well-deserved rest and recovery. Enjoy the hotel pool, a hot bath, and a 90-minute deep tissue massage to soothe the muscles after the hike
day_by_day.evening: Quiet and relaxing evening in Ubud — browse the night market stalls at Ubud Market or enjoy a gentle evening walk along the ridge

meals.breakfast: Light pre-hike snack pack prepared by the hotel — energy bars, bananas, and a thermos of Balinese coffee
meals.lunch: Late brunch upon return — eggs Benedict, acai bowl, and fresh coconut water at the hotel or at Kafe in Ubud
meals.dinner: Dinner at Three Monkeys Restaurant Ubud — romantic candlelit setting in a rice field, serving Indonesian and international cuisine with excellent cocktails

day_by_day.notes: The Mount Batur sunrise trek requires a certified guide — arrange through the hotel. Temperatures at the summit can drop to 10–15°C so bring a warm layer. The early start is demanding but the experience is extraordinary.

day_by_day.morning: Indulgent wellness morning — begin with a gentle morning flow yoga session, followed by a full COMO Shambhala Estate Wellness Experience or a premium spa day at Fivelements Retreat — Bali's most acclaimed holistic wellness resort on the banks of the Ayung River
day_by_day.afternoon: White water rafting on the Ayung River — a thrilling yet accessible 2-hour rafting experience through the jungle gorge with stunning waterfall views. Suitable for all fitness levels
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset cocktails at the hotel terrace, reflecting on the journey with a glass of Champagne overlooking the Campuhan Ridge

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel — full Balinese spread with nasi goreng, fresh fruits, pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Fivelements' Sakti Dining Room — a stunning riverside restaurant serving raw, living, and plant-based cuisine inspired by Balinese healing traditions
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Locavore — Ubud's most celebrated fine-dining restaurant, consistently ranked among Asia's best. Multi-course tasting menu with wine pairing showcasing Indonesian ingredients with world-class technique

day_by_day.notes: Locavore requires reservations weeks in advance — book immediately upon trip confirmation. The Ayung River rafting can be arranged through the hotel and typically includes hotel pickup and return. Fivelements is a 20-minute drive from the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga and meditation on the Campuhan Ridge — a mindful farewell to Ubud. Slow morning walk through the ridge with gratitude journaling at a viewpoint
day_by_day.afternoon: Checkout and last-minute shopping in Ubud for artisan gifts — handwoven textiles, silver jewelry from Celuk, and local organic beauty products. Private transfer to the airport
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the serenity of Bali home

meals.breakfast: Final luxurious breakfast at the hotel — choose your favorites from the full menu, savoring the last moments in the Campuhan setting
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or a quick stop at a Seminyak café en route — Revolver Espresso for excellent coffee and a bite
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Check-out is typically at 12:00 noon — arrange a late checkout if your flight allows. Allow at least 3 hours for the drive to the airport from Ubud during peak hours. Store luggage at the hotel while doing final shopping. Request a packed snack bag from the hotel for the journey.

query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA
